title: Who Should Be The Next Bond, My 'Nemesis,' Three Movies To Get To Know Me and 29 Other Questions Answered
text:
Friday! Shea Serrano and I are going to be talking about all things James Bond casting on Substack Live Friday at 4 pm. Mark your calendars!
For this year’s annual B’DAY AMA, no one asked me how I hope The Morning Show ends, so I will answer that for you here and not count it as one of the 32 questions. I think we unfortunately will relitigate the death of Steve Carell and somehow the president dies, and it becomes a constitutional crisis, and somehow the president becomes Jennifer Aniston but she’s assassinated by that Duplass brother in a murder suicide bc he remembered that he’s in love with her, so then Reese Witherspoon becomes president, and Mia Jordan becomes her Secretary of State and Cory woos her and that becomes a whole other editorial crisis for UBN and he leaves the network to become First Husband, and as First Husband he starts a band in his spare time and that band makes the song that is The Morning Show’s theme. Voila!
If you could write a ‘Being John Malkovich’-esque film starring an actor as themselves for our gen, which actor would you choose? Your mind… what an incredible question. First thought is Robert Pattinson. Second thought is Tyler, The Creator. Randomly, Kirsten Dunst? I would watch the hell out of any of those.
More on the Jeremy Strong email pls. It was a line from Dante’s Inferno that he felt was “apposite both for the whole season for me but especially for the finale in Italy.” Apposite — a word I had to look up obviously and loved.
What celebrity ex-couple do you think has the greatest chance of pulling off a Bennifer 2.0 (and it can’t be Bennifer 3.0 lol)? Maybe Brad Pitt and Jennifer Aniston. We are talking about a man who made a press tour out of announcing his sobriety to get over bad PR from his divorce and is now making a press tour out of announcing that he’s drinking again to open a movie that appears to be MAGA Cast Away, but instead of a volleyball it’s a dog. He’s trying anything!
I feel like you’ve spoken about this before but were you always planning to be a dog mom or did Remy just fall into your life? What’s your favorite part of her being in your life? I wanted a dog after I dogsat for my friend Keith and his dog Fenty on and off one summer during COVID. I can’t remember exactly how I decided to get a dog! But I was first on a list for her litter, and I just knew she was my girl. She had one big pretty curl right in the middle of her forehead.
I know that everyone thinks they have the perfect dog, but she really is the funniest little-big personality: nosy, bossy, a huge flirt. (I wonder where she gets it from! She is definitely a dog raised on RHONY and Succession…) Maybe the most special thing about Remy is that she got to spend a lot of time with both Auntie and Granny before they died, and having her makes me feel really connected to them.You recently moved. What’s the first non-essential item you unpacked? What a good question. I am having to really think about the definition of essential, because everything feels essential to me. Probably my old journals! And my purses.
I wanna know about the therapy revelation AND the Broadway show. The therapy revelation is that I learned growing up that my job isn’t to collaborate, it’s to project manage. The Broadway show was Titanique :/
Curious what your current writing process is and if the Artist’s Way really did something to you. I have recently come to terms with the fact that I am no longer “doing the Artist’s Way” but “need to restart the Artist’s Way.” I got stuck on week three or four and kept losing track. I still do my morning pages every morning; I could be a little more strict about making time for my own Artist Dates.
I liked it though! I can see how the God stuff can be a little bit othering (I grew up in Oklahoma… didn’t phase me at all). My idea of divinity has a lot to do with creativity, though, so it worked for me. I appreciated thinking about my inner child as a way to court the muse. Some of it is a bit too geared to people who come to writing after/during other careers; some of that stuff didn’t apply to me at all, but I found it really compelling to think of myself as a novice writer, or a writer trying on a different practice.
My writing process is pretty standard. I wake up in the morning with a ton of good ideas fighting to get out of me. By 1 or 2 in the afternoon, all those good ideas have started to rot. I can’t work through the stench — that’s when I see a movie or have a Zoom or do something to give my tired midday brain a jolt. I don’t brick but DND really helps. Most of these newsletters are written in one sitting, and then I read it the next day (or a few hours later) to decide if I really think it’s funny enough to warrant your attention. I’ve started going to bed earlier, around 10:30, but I sometimes get a lot of inspiration around 8 or 9 and can work till midnight if I feel in the mood. The most important part of my process is trying not to fight myself too much. Sometimes I do my best work at the desk; sometimes it’s horizontal on the sofa. It blows my confidence if I try to force myself to have a good idea at 3 pm when I don’t have it in me.Who is your pick for the next Bond? (If you care lol) I care deeply!
Shea SerranoofGOOD MOVIEand I are actually going to be talking about our dream Bond casting on Substack Live Friday at 4 pm. Mark your calendars! Potential names thrown around the trades have been Jacob Elordi, Paul Mescal, etc. But I am convinced I have thought of the right man for the job… and no, it’s not who you’re thinking.How did you get into journalism and writing for NYMag? I’m a starving, wannabe freelance journalist — and it’s so hard to get my foot in the door! Any advice would be so helpful! I read all of your contributing articles : )
